output.summary: KEP-5040 proposes removing the in-tree gitRepo volume driver from kubelet while keeping gitRepo volumes in the Kubernetes API. Pods with gitRepo volumes would still be admitted by kube-apiserver, but kubelets with the GitRepoVolumeDriver gate off would fail them with an error. Status is implementable at stage disabled.
output.rationale: gitRepo volumes can be exploited for remote code execution as root on nodes (CVE-2024-10220), and the driver is deprecated, unmaintained, and rarely used. Maintainers chose to disable it by default behind a feature gate first, then lock and remove it after a feedback period, rather than wait for a full removal. The discussion says this accelerated plan was chosen because disabling old code faster carries no risk of enabling untested code.

alternatives.option: Remove gitRepo from the Kubernetes API as well
alternatives.why_not: Explicitly a non-goal in the KEP; pods with gitRepo volumes are still admitted by kube-apiserver and fail in kubelet.

alternatives.option: Remove the driver and silently ignore gitRepo volumes
alternatives.why_not: Thockin asked whether to silently ignore or fail in kubelet; liggitt said if a pod needs this volume and the plugin is disabled, the kubelet should fail it, and the design chose failing.

alternatives.option: Follow the slower path: keep the driver enabled, then lock and remove it over several releases
alternatives.why_not: Liggitt argued that a security hole stays open until the default is disabled, so the team agreed to skip ahead to off-by-default in 1.33 with an escape hatch.

alternatives.option: Disable only the hooks (the attack vector) via a new field
alternatives.why_not: Mentioned only as a fallback if there is real pushback; not the chosen plan.

evidence.quote: kubelets with the feature-gate GitRepoVolumeDriver set to false will not run them and return an appropriate error to the user
gitRepo volume types can be exploited to gain remote code execution as root on the nodes as shown in
since there's a security hole that doesn't get closed by default until step 2, and there's no risk of accelerating to step 2
I think the only bits that are urgent are 1) disabling by default with an escape hatch and 2) starting the process to drive feedback
the feature gate is deprecated and locked to false in 1.36, the only thing we need to do in 1.37 is to update the KEP to set milestone to "stable: 1.37"
